requirement: server-side object ownership/permission check exists on every read/write route
architecture_reasoning: Traced the request/response path in app/orders/views.py: the handler derives the authenticated user from the trusted session (request.user), loads the Order record by primary key from the URL, and compares order.owner_id == request.user.id before returning or mutating the record. No client-supplied field overrides this check.
call_chain: HTTP request -> auth middleware (session) -> OrdersView.get/post -> Order.objects.get(pk=order_id) -> ownership check -> response

evidence_references.detail: DELETE handler at line 58 has no ownership check before order.delete()

result_reasoning: app/orders/views.py:58 (the DELETE handler) loads the Order by primary key and calls .delete() immediately with no ownership/permission check at all -- any authenticated user can delete any other user's order by guessing or incrementing the numeric id.
